COMPUTER NETWORKS · TRANSPORT LAYER
TCP AND UDPIN COMPUTER NETWORKS
How applications exchange data, and why reliability and latency lead to 
different choices.
Seminar overview · connection, delivery, and trade-offs

01 · THE TRANSPORT LAYER
The transport layer connects applications
IP moves packets between hosts; the transport layer moves data between applications on those hosts. Port numbers 
identify the sending and receiving applications. TCP and UDP sit above IP and below application protocols.
Application
Web, video, games, DNS
Transport
TCP or UDP
Ports and delivery behavior
Network
IP addresses and routing
Application data becomes transport segments or datagrams, then IP packets.
02

TCP · TRANSMISSION CONTROL PROTOCOL
RELIABLEDELIVERY
OVERHEAD IS THE TRADE
TCP trades overhead 
for reliability
Connection-oriented
TCP establishes a connection before application 
data flows.
Reliable and ordered
Sequence numbers, acknowledgements, and 
retransmission help deliver complete data in 
order.
Familiar example
Loading a web page or transferring a file favors 
correctness over the smallest possible delay.

05 · UDP · USER DATAGRAM PROTOCOL
UDP keeps communication 
lightweight
UDP is connectionless: independent datagrams need no session.
Low overhead
Small headers and no handshake mean fast setup.
Few built-in guarantees
UDP does not promise delivery, ordering, or retransmission.
Online gaming
Online gaming favors fresh positions over recovered old updates.
07

06 · UDP DELIVERY
UDP sends datagrams without retransmission
CLIENT
Send
Datagrams leave 
independently.
DATAGRAM 1  →   ROUTER  →   SERVER
DATAGRAM 2  →   ROUTER  →   SERVER
DATAGRAM 3  →   ROUTER  ✕  LOST
SERVER
Continue
No built-in retransmission. The 
application decides what to do 
next.
The trade-off: less waiting and less overhead, with less delivery control.
